---
title: "Research"
---

David's work sits at the intersection of education policy and economics, using large administrative datasets and, where possible, experimental or quasi-experimental designs to understand what makes teachers and teaching effective — and how policy can help recruit, develop, and retain a more effective and more diverse teacher workforce. This page draws on his July 2025 CV plus more recent publications; the [CV](cv.qmd) and [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=atIXv0UAAAAJ&hl=en) remain the most complete record. Below: what's currently in progress, the published record it builds on, how that work gets funded, and where else David is active in the field.

## Beyond His Own Studies

David also contributes to the field's shared infrastructure and gatekeeping. He directs the [Maryland Equity Project](https://education.umd.edu/research/centers/mep) and serves as principal investigator for the research branch of the [Maryland Longitudinal Data System](https://mldscenter.maryland.gov/), both housed at UMD, and holds an affiliate appointment in the School of Public Policy. He's a research affiliate of the [CALDER Center](https://caldercenter.org/experts/david-blazar), and sits on the editorial boards of the *Journal of Research on Educational Effectiveness* (2025–present) and *Educational Researcher* (2021–present).
